name: Maneuver Planning Plugin
description: Orbital maneuver planning over the $MPL (maneuver plan) standard: classical transfers, Lambert, phasing, relative-motion (ROE) targeting, collision avoidance, approach corridors, closed-loop rendezvous and orbit geometry. One $MPL request in, the same $MPL answered out.

sequentialJustification.detail: Every operation this module exposes is a closed form, a scalar root-find over a handful of doubles, or a bounded integer scan over one of those: a Hohmann transfer is four sqrt() calls, the most expensive root-find (the universal-variable Lambert solve) converges in single-digit iterations, and the only loop whose trip count a caller influences is phasingFromTargetState's revolution-count recommendation, which evaluates one closed form per revolution and whose ceiling is CLAMPED into [1, 100000] rather than trusted — a hostile maxRevs is a typo, not a workload. There is nothing here to shard — the work per invoke is microseconds, and spawning a thread would cost more than the answer. Parallelism over maneuvers belongs to the CALLER, which plans many independent burns; this module holds no cross-call state (its only static is the per-invoke fault latch, cleared at entry), so any number of instances may be driven concurrently by a host that wants throughput. Both thread models compile through the same clang wasm32-wasip1-threads toolchain; this one links no thread-spawn contract because it genuinely never spawns.

methods.description: Solves the problem a $MPL request names (PROBLEM plus the matching REQUEST sub-table, km / km/s / deg units) and answers with the same $MPL: the request echoed, PLANNER and STATUS set, and the burns, arcs, totals, options and the problem's solution detail filled. A request the planner refuses is answered with STATUS and ERROR_CODE/ERROR_MESSAGE on the plan and the same reason as the invoke error; no input traps the module.

inputPorts.description: $MPL request: PROBLEM and REQUEST filled, result fields empty.

outputPorts.description: $MPL answer: the request echoed with STATUS, BURNS, ARCS, TOTAL_DELTA_V_KM_S, TOTAL_TIME_S, SOLVER, OPTIONS, TRAJECTORY and the PHASING / RELATIVE / RENDEZVOUS / GEOMETRY detail of the problem.
